Valve actuators will be suitable for the valve types chosen, whether quarter‐turn (e.g., ball valves) or gate valves. Depending upon valve size and power availability, actuators will be motor operated and supplied by three‐phase (e.g., 480 VAC, 60 Hz) or by split phase (e.g., 230 VAC, 60 Hz). Actuator size/horsepower will be selected based upon closing and breakaway torque needs and required speed of valve closure. Special attention shall be given to valve material selection where high differential pressure may be generated, specifically for blowdown and equalization valves. Sacrificial valves may be considered for these applications with permanently installed isolation valves between any sacrificial components and the pipeline. Isolation valves of 10” and larger sizes will be equipped with actuators. All actuated valves shall be ordered with provision for remote actuation and position indication. 6.2 DEPTH OF COVER Minimum depth of cover shall be 6 feet throughout the pipeline system and increased to 5 feet in cultivated fields. Cover depths for specific crossings can be found in those respective sections. Depth of cover may be increased if determined to be necessary based on landowner input. 6.3 PIPELINE APPURTENANCES 6.3.1 Launcher & Receivers All Launcher and Receiver installations are to be designed in accordance with 49 CFR, Part 195, Sub‐Part F – Operation and Maintenance, Paragraph 195.426 and Project Specifications. Barred tees shall be installed along all mainline branch connections which are greater than or equal to half the size of the line pipe, to facilitate pigging. Valves used on launchers and receivers will be above ground. Trap valves of 12” and larger sizes will have electrically powered actuators. Facility and pipeline design will account for size and workspace requirements for pigging activities. ILI tool selection shall be evaluated during the Detailed Design phase and this document will be updated to identify bend radius limits, and any configuration restrictions (such as minimum length between bends) by line size. Launcher/Receiver design is to accommodate the nominal diameter pipe section and will also be made long‐enough to handle the full length of the ILI tools. This is to ensure that ILI tools will pass far enough into the over‐sized barrel so that the tail end of the ILI tool will be positioned safely Page 11 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 downstream of the main trap block valve – allowing it to be fully‐closed for barrel isolation and tool removal purposes 6.3.2 Pipe, Flanges and Fittings Steel grade for pipe will be confirmed during the FEED phase of the project based on design pressure requirements and economic evaluation of yield strength versus wall thickness for each line size. Deviations from the preferred pipeline specifications may be considered in the event existing pipe meeting the design pressure requirements is sourced.
